subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Birth of Formula One
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Birth of Formula One.

hook.text: In 1950, the FIA created a World Championship for drivers—Formula One was officially born.

buildup.text: The first championship race was held at Silverstone, a converted World War II airfield in England.

discovery.text: Giuseppe Farina won the inaugural title driving an Alfa Romeo at an average speed of 90 mph.

twist.text: Early F1 cars had no seatbelts—drivers preferred being thrown clear rather than trapped in a fire.

climax.text: From that airfield start, F1 grew into the most watched annual sporting series on the planet.

punchline.text: The world's fastest sport started on a runway.

quiz.question: Where was the first Formula One championship race held?

details.summary: The FIA established the Formula One World Championship in 1950, with the first race held at Silverstone, creating the premier international single-seater racing series that continues to this day.
details.whyItMatters: Formula One became the pinnacle of automotive technology and global sporting entertainment, driving decades of innovation while attracting billions of viewers and reshaping motorsport culture worldwide.
takeaways: The first championship race was at Silverstone on May 13, 1950
Giuseppe Farina won the inaugural World Championship
The series unified existing Grand Prix races under one championship

faq.question: What were the original rules of Formula One?
faq.answer: Cars were limited to 4.5-liter naturally aspirated or 1.5-liter supercharged engines. Seven races counted toward the championship, including the Indianapolis 500. Regulations have changed dramatically since.

faq.question: Why is it called Formula One?
faq.answer: The formula refers to the set of rules teams must follow when building their cars. The One designates it as the top tier, distinguishing it from lower formulae like Formula Two and Formula Three.
